newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Top Korean industry group blasts Thomson decision.
newsitem.headline: Top Korean industry group blasts Thomson decision.

text.p: South Korea's top industry group attacked France on Wednesday for scuttling the sale of Thomson Multimedia to a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Group, which has vowed not to give up on the sale.

The Federation of Korean Industries released a statement saying it had sent a letter to the French ambassador in Seoul that "expressed worries about the French government's discriminatory practices towards non-European companies".
"We also expressed the shock and regret of the South Korean business community concerning the decision made on non-economic grounds and for reasons that cannot be understood," the statement added.
A Daewoo official, meanwhile, reiterated the company's determination not to walk away from the issue.

"Yes, we still want to take Thomson over," Daewoo Electronics Co vice president Nam Kwi-hyen said at a European businessmen's luncheon in Seoul. "But we have to wait for the French government's decision."
France last week suspended the sale of consumer-electronics firm Thomson Multimedia, a unit of state-owned electronics giant Thomson SA, to Daewoo Electronics, provoking an outcry in South Korea.
The South Korean government and industry groups have rallied behind Daewoo over the decision, which some South Korean media have portrayed as racist.
French sources yesterday said France planned to unveil new terms for the privatisation of Thomson SA this week.
Nam repeated Daewoo's pledge to add 5,000 new jobs at Thomson.
"There's no reason to worry about any change in working conditions and welfare in the future," he said.
He said he believed French labour unions would drop their opposition once they "see that the favourable outcome (of a Daewoo takeover) is in their best interest and the best way to secure growth".
The federation, which represents South Korea's mighty business conglomerates known as "chaebol", later released an English version of its letter to Ambassador Dominique Perreau.
French businessmen in South Korea are worried the Thomson fiasco could sour the business atmosphere.

South Korea plans to spend billions of dollars upgrading infrastructure and modernising its armed forces over the next several years, and French companies are well placed to pick up contracts for nuclear power plants, railway equipment and possibly fighter jets.
The letter noted that French and Korean business cooperation was in a "golden age", and said the timing of the French decision was unfortunate.
The Anglo-French consortium GEC-Alsthom won a $22.1 billion contract in 1994 to supply the TGV high-speed train in South Korea. The French company Framatome sells nuclear power plants there.
France is also trying to sell Dassault Aviation's Rafale combat planes to Seoul, which plans to spend $24 billion to upgrade its defences by 2010.
